rounds.response: Counsel — Your proposed “joint” pretrial is unacceptable: it materially misstates the record, omits and rewrites contract provisions your client has already admitted, refuses to stipulate to authenticity of core business records, and seeks to cut from the exhibit list the documents that prove your client’s misuse of our IP. By 5:00 p.m. PST two business days from receipt you must (1) restore and admit the governing contract language as previously produced, (2) stipulate to authenticity of the business records produced (Bates [insert ranges]) and the chain-of-custody for key device images, and (3) add the disputed IP-misuse documents to your exhibit list — otherwise we will treat your draft as an intentional refusal to meet the court’s pretrial obligations. If you do not cure, we will, within the seven-day pretrial window, file motions to compel and to deem authentic/admissible business records (Fed. R. Civ. P. 37), motions in limine to admit key documents and strike your last-minute carve-outs, a motion to expand our exhibit/witness lists and to exclude undisclosed evidence, and motions for fees and sanctions under Rule 11, 28 U.S.C. § 1927 and the court’s inherent authority. We will also lodge our own joint pretrial statement with Judge Hartman exposing these mischaracterizations and will seek expedited relief; call me within 24 hours if you intend to avoid this escalation.
